source_snapshot.procedure: Install two DIMM types but lists copied CPU attributes—QPI speeds, speeds, power and cores—then attempt boot and inspect DIMM information/BMC logs.
source_snapshot.criteria: System does not boot; BMC and post-recovery UEFI SEL report unsupported DIMMs; copied wording says `between the Boot CPUs`; physical lightpath identifies failing DIMM(s) and System Fault LED is on.
source_snapshot.script: No script; physical memory service is required.
source_snapshot.deepseek: NO; keeps physical swap manual but does not reconcile copied CPU semantics or define a DIMM-specific oracle.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION with exact DIMM pair, one controlled mismatch, topology, qualified technician, OOB evidence and recovery.

old_problem: The source's intent is a DIMM-mixing rejection test, but its examples QPI, core count and `between the Boot CPUs` are copied CPU language and cannot select a memory fixture or PASS oracle. It also assumes every two-type combination must fail, although many platforms permit selected mixed capacities/ranks/speeds with downclocking. The core coverage can nevertheless be recovered safely by requiring an exact platform-documented, electrically/key-compatible but explicitly prohibited DIMM population as Project configuration, plus slot-specific event/indicator and recovery oracles.
disposition_reason: Resolve the copied CPU terms in the Review layer without changing Master: test one exact pair of individually supported, electrically/mechanically compatible DIMMs whose combined placement is explicitly prohibited by the target platform memory-population specification for one named attribute/matrix rule. A qualified technician performs powered-down ESD-controlled installation and restoration; automation only reads inventory, POST/training, raw BMC/UEFI events and health. Require a documented reject-at-training/no-boot outcome for that exact fixture, slot-mapped DIMM event, human photos of every fitted lightpath/fault indicator, and complete restoration to the captured supported topology. Missing part numbers/slots/event bytes are bounded Project configuration and yield NOT READY; arbitrary DIMMs, individually unsupported modules, unsafe voltage/keying, inferred non-boot, CPU events or repeat attempts are forbidden.
decision_basis: Master XLSX rows 1424-1427, exact same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT second review, tests.json, selection manifest and historical V3.1 record were directly read. Row 1424 is the separate Mismatched CPUs case and row 1425 the separate individually unsupported-DIMMs case, so neither may cross-credit this mixed-but-individually-supported pair. Formal queue sequence 90 was read from the locked queue and verified as row 1433 / variant 937cfeeea4f3936c.

QPI/link speed and core count are processor properties, not DIMM attributes. `Between the Boot CPUs` also describes the separate CPU mismatch case. The Review layer records those phrases as source conflict and replaces them only with DIMM-specific inventory/population evidence.

A meaningful mismatch fixture uses two exact part numbers that are each supported in isolation but whose simultaneous population/placement is explicitly forbidden by the exact server/BIOS memory population guide. Otherwise a failure could be ordinary unsupported-module coverage from row 1425 rather than mismatch coverage.

The mismatch dimension must be electrically and mechanically safe. Different keying/technology/voltage that should not physically fit is not a test invitation; the technician never forces a module. Approved dimensions may include a documented prohibited mixing rule for capacity, organization, rank, data rate, vendor/3DS/persistent-memory class or channel symmetry as the target guide specifies.

Different supported speed bins do not universally imply no boot; firmware may train at a common lower speed. The Project matrix must explicitly predict rejection for the chosen pair and slots. If the platform documents supported downclock/mixing, this no-boot fixture is invalid rather than a FAILing DUT.
The no-boot oracle needs a named training/POST stage, console/POST code and approved deadline. Request failure, network ping or operator waiting alone cannot prove memory-training rejection.

IPMI defines generic Memory sensor/event structures, while DMTF Redfish Memory exposes inventory/location attributes. Neither defines this platform's prohibited mix, exact raw event bytes, DIMM locator mapping or physical LED behavior; those remain target SPEC inputs rather than Engineering Decision Pending.

BMC OOB evidence is essential while OS/UEFI interfaces are unavailable. After the technician restores the supported layout, UEFI SEL can corroborate the event, but a CPU event or generic no-boot cannot replace a slot-specific DIMM mismatch record.

Lightpath and System Fault LED are physical evidence. A human must capture genuine photos/video tied to timestamp and slot. An absent option is N/A only from chassis/platform configuration authority; an API field or simulated locate LED cannot substitute.

Power removal, standby discharge, ESD, slot orientation/latch and DIMM handling follow the exact service manual. The source's generic log clear is rejected because baseline/failure events must remain distinguishable; no automatic second boot attempt is allowed.

ED-02 preserves separate CPU/unsupported/mismatch identities; ED-15 requires SPEC-backed applicability/N/A; ED-17/ED-25 keep physical work operator-controlled; ED-19 preserves logs; ED-20/ED-23 require real visual correlation; ED-29 requires explicit boot state; ED-30/ED-34 permit exact Project parameters; ED-38 prohibits retry and agent verdicts.

test_case.test_name: Platform-documented mismatched DIMM pair: manual installation, memory-training rejection, slot events and recovery
test_case.purpose: Verify one explicitly prohibited mixed-DIMM population using two individually supported modules, including the target's memory-training rejection, DIMM/slot BMC and post-recovery UEFI events, genuine physical fault indicators and restoration to a healthy supported topology without substituting CPU mismatch or individually unsupported-DIMM coverage.
required_package: Exact server/board/CPU/BIOS/BMC/CPLD identities and versioned memory population/compatibility specification identifying one prohibited mixed pair/placement and its expected reject state

Two exact test DIMMs individually listed as supported: manufacturer/PN/serial, DDR generation/form factor/key/voltage, capacity, organization, ranks, data rate/timings, ECC/3DS/persistent-memory attributes and SPD hashes; exact socket/channel/slot map and one controlled forbidden combination
Known-good supported recovery topology with every DIMM/blank/airflow part mapped by slot/serial, plus pre-test Redfish/SMBIOS/SPD/BMC inventory and memory/ECC/thermal health

Qualified memory technician, target service manual, complete power removal/standby discharge, ESD controls, latch/orientation/torque/airflow instructions, maintenance window and immediate physical-action authorization

Authoritative training/POST stage and deadline, console/POST-code capture, exact raw BMC/UEFI DIMM event and slot decode, fitted lightpath/System Fault LED map, BMC OOB access and protected evidence storage
test_case.test_command: HYBRID MANUAL PROCEDURE; DO NOT EXECUTE DURING REVIEW. Record Source Key/variant and capture/hash the healthy supported topology: every slot/PN/serial/SPD, Redfish/SMBIOS/BMC inventory, memory capacity/mode/ECC/thermals, console/POST, raw BMC SEL and genuine indicator baseline without clearing logs. Validate from the target SPEC that DIMM A and B are each supported, physically/electrically compatible, and only their named combination/placement is prohibited with expected memory-training rejection; reject QPI/core/CPU criteria. Power the SUT fully off per service guide, remove AC/standby as required and prove de-energized. After immediate confirmation, the qualified technician installs the exact pair in the named slots under ESD controls and records photos/serials/latches; the agent performs no physical step. Make one controlled power-on attempt and collect synchronized BMC OOB, console/POST/training timeline and raw events until the approved rejection deadline. A human records all fitted lightpath and System Fault indicators. Do not retry. Power off safely; technician restores the exact supported slot/serial topology and airflow hardware. Boot once through POST to OS Ready, collect BMC plus UEFI SEL without clearing, and require restored inventory/capacity/mode/ECC/thermals/indicators/health. Preserve row-1424 CPU mismatch and row-1425 unsupported DIMM as separate cases.
test_case.expected_result: For the exact platform-prohibited mixed pair, the single boot attempt stops at the documented memory-training/POST stage within the approved deadline and does not reach OS Ready. BMC emits the exact DIMM-specific event mapped to the expected slot/channel; post-recovery UEFI SEL corroborates it; every fitted lightpath/fault indicator shows the specified genuine state. After restoring the supported topology, one boot reaches OS Ready and exact DIMM inventory, usable capacity, memory mode, ECC/thermal health and physical indicators return to baseline with no unrelated errors. A platform that permits the mix/downclocks is a bad fixture and NOT READY, not a DUT FAIL.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires exact Source Key/variant, two individually supported DIMMs, authoritative one-rule prohibited-mix matrix, correct slots, qualified powered-down service, one boot attempt, documented training-stage rejection/no OS Ready, exact slot-specific raw BMC and post-recovery UEFI events, human visual evidence for every fitted indicator, exact supported-layout restoration and full OS/memory/ECC/thermal recovery. FAIL covers boot contrary to a valid reject SPEC, wrong/missing DIMM event/slot/indicator, unsafe electrical/mechanical condition, collateral error or incomplete recovery. NOT READY covers missing pair/slot/SPEC/event/indicator/timeout/technician/recovery inputs, a combination actually supported by downclocking, or individually unsupported DIMMs. N/A requires authoritative absence of mismatch rejection applicability, not missing parts. CPU events, row-1425 results, generic no-boot or retry cannot pass.
safety_gate: All DIMM removal/insertion, latch and physical LED work is human-only. The qualified technician follows exact power-off, AC/standby discharge, ESD, orientation and service-manual procedures; the agent never directs hands-on motion.
Use only a documented safe, key-compatible mixed pair. Never force a keyed module, mix unsafe voltage/technology, probe arbitrary combinations or use production/customer memory.
Verify both modules are individually supported and the pair/placement alone is prohibited. This prevents collapsing row 1425 unsupported-module coverage into this mismatch case.
Preserve logs and first-failure state. Do not clear BMC/UEFI/OS evidence, automatically retry training, change slots after failure or power-cycle to seek a preferred event.

Abort on arcing/odor/heat, damaged socket/latch, wrong part/slot, unexpected power/rail/thermal state, BMC loss or training behavior outside the approved contract; safely de-energize and inspect before restoration.
A human captures actual lightpath/System Fault evidence. API/SEL/locate commands do not substitute, and absent indicators require authoritative configuration-backed N/A.

Restore exact known-good slot/serial/airflow hardware and verify full training, OS Ready, capacity/mode/ECC/thermals/SEL/indicators before release. No second mismatch attempt without a new review/run.
expected_evidence: Exact Source Key/variant; server/board/CPU/BIOS/BMC/CPLD identities; cited memory population rule; separate CPU and unsupported-DIMM identities
DIMM A/B PN/serial/SPD hashes and decoded attributes, proof each is individually supported, exact single prohibited mix dimension and slot/channel topology
Known-good baseline/recovery layout and Redfish/SMBIOS/BMC inventory, capacity/mode/ECC/thermal health, raw logs and physical indicator baseline
Technician identity, service/ESD/power isolation checklist, point-of-action approval and timestamped photos of exact modules/slots/latches
Single boot/training timeline, console/POST code, BMC power state, raw/decoded DIMM event and slot correlation, genuine lightpath/System Fault photos
Restoration photos, post-recovery BMC/UEFI SEL correlation, exact DIMM inventory/capacity/mode/ECC/thermal/indicator state and OS Ready; explicit no-retry/no-DUT-action-by-review-agent statement
test_case.recovery: Before the mismatch attempt, stage the exact supported slot/serial topology and service checklist. On the expected or any abnormal training stop, preserve BMC/console/visual evidence and do not retry. Remove power/standby per the service guide; the technician removes only the test pair, inspects sockets/latches/modules and restores the known-good modules and airflow hardware to the recorded slots. If mechanical, electrical or thermal damage is suspected, quarantine the platform rather than power it. Perform one approved recovery boot, verify inventory, capacity/mode, ECC/thermals, BMC/UEFI SEL, indicators and OS Ready. Any persistent fault remains FAIL and is escalated without another mismatch configuration.

source_conflict.reason: The title and principal criteria unambiguously target DIMM mismatch. Review-layer correction removes copied CPU-only QPI/core/Boot-CPU wording and binds one DIMM-specific prohibited-mix matrix, event and slot oracle without altering Master or reducing physical/visual coverage.

blocked.reason: No irreducible command or hardware behavior must be guessed: exact DIMM pair/slots/reject rule/events/indicators are explicit target configuration prerequisites. Missing inputs yield NOT READY and no physical action.

project_authority: The platform memory/BIOS/BMC owners choose the two individually supported modules, prohibited combination/slots, training/event/indicator oracle and recovery topology; the chassis owner authorizes service. They cannot translate QPI/cores into DIMM attributes, use unsafe/key-incompatible parts, assume all mixed speeds fail, substitute CPU/unsupported-DIMM evidence, waive genuine indicator photos, clear logs or authorize retry.
